## What does it mean to say a package supports AD?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
- We do not think there is a community standard for what supporting
  automatic differentiation means
- So we aimed to build our own, using `DifferentiationInterfaceTest`

::: {.callout-note}
Is there a guide for any of this anywhere in the Julia ecosystem? I went
looking and did not find one.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```julia
const _AD_BACKENDS = [
  (header = "ForwardDiff", ...),
  (header = "ReverseDiff (tape)", ...),
  (header = "ReverseDiff (compiled)", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme forward", ...),
  (header = "Enzyme reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake reverse", ...),
  (header = "Mooncake forward", ...),
]
```

::: {.attribution}
Abridged from `_AD_BACKENDS`, `src/scaffold.jl` in
[EpiAwarePackageTools.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/EpiAwarePackageTools.jl),
read 2026-08-12. The list generates the CI matrix, the Codecov flags, the
README badges and the support table in the docs ·
[DifferentiationInterfaceTest.jl](https://github.com/JuliaDiff/DifferentiationInterface.jl).
:::
